problem: Existing robot learning surveys focus on a single task and mostly cover traditional methods (IL/RL). There is no comprehensive review of foundation-model-based robot learning across tasks.
motivation: Foundation models, especially LLMs and multimodal models, promise to fix traditional robot learning's weak generalization, adaptability, planning and reasoning, but the work is new and scattered. A systematic taxonomy is needed to guide future research.
key_idea: A survey that traces the evolution of robot learning, covers preliminaries (simulators, datasets, foundation models), and organizes foundation-model-based work into manipulation, navigation, task planning and reasoning, plus open challenges.
insight: This is a survey with no experiments or ablations. Its main argument is that current foundation models are strong at high-level semantics but weak at low-level control and dynamics data. The authors argue future progress needs dynamic and interaction data, robot-specific foundation models, hardware/software decoupling, and alignment.
method: Technical evolution: reviews teaching programming (kinesthetic teaching, teleoperation), RL, embodied imitation learning, and generative-model-based learning.
Preliminaries: summarizes simulators, static vs dynamic datasets, and foundation models, in appendix tables.
Manipulation: covers skill primitives, complex manipulation tasks, and multimodal fusion (vision, touch, audio).
Navigation: covers environment perception, map creation, localization and motion planning (VLMaps, NavGPT, VLN-BERT, etc.).
Task planning: covers single-robot decomposition, multi-robot planning, and self-correction and self-improvement.
Reasoning: covers logical, commonsense, affordance and personalized reasoning.
Discussion: hardware/software decoupling, dynamic data, generalization, multimodal interaction, exclusive robot foundation models, computation efficiency, safety and ethics.
numbers_note: Survey paper; no experimental results reported.
results: It provides a taxonomy over four robot-learning areas (manipulation, navigation, planning, reasoning) with datasets and metrics per area. It identifies seven open challenges. No quantitative results.
limitations: Navigation coverage is shallow and mixes VLN, object navigation and localization without comparing quantitative results.
Coverage is mostly literature up to late 2023 and is largely descriptive, with no comparison tables in the main text.
Some areas (LLM self-correction, code generation, knowledge graphs) are only loosely tied to robotics.
